D: A New York fashion designer goes home to Alabama to divorce the husband she never told anyone about.
P: Serve the mains when Melanie sits down at her parents' table back home.
S: Melanie's home town of Pigeon Creek
Green tomatoes sliced thick, dipped in egg and cornmeal, fried until golden, served with a lemony remoulade.

Cornmeal, flour, buttermilk, egg and melted butter mixed briefly, baked in a hot cast iron pan at 220C for 20 minutes, with honey butter. Put a 25cm cast iron pan with 20g butter into the oven at 220C to heat. Mix 150g cornmeal, 120g plain flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder and half a teaspoon salt. Whisk in 300ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g melted butter until just combined. Pour into the hot pan so it sizzles and bake 20 minutes until golden. Beat 80g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of salt and serve with warm wedges.
the local bar where Jake drinks
Pecans tossed with melted butter, brown sugar and a pinch of cayenne, roasted at 170C for 12 minutes until glossy.
M: Pigeon Creek cornmeal fish and slaw

Flathead fillets dipped in buttermilk and crunchy cayenne cornmeal, fried crisp, with a tangy buttermilk slaw, hot sauce and lemon. Mix 100g cornmeal, 50g plain flour, 1 tsp paprika, half a teaspoon cayenne and salt. Dip 700g flathead fillets in 200ml buttermilk, then press into the cornmeal. Shallow fry in 1cm of oil at 180C for 2 to 3 minutes a side until crisp. For slaw, toss a quarter each of green and red cabbage, finely shredded, and 1 grated carrot with 100ml buttermilk, 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp cider vinegar and 1 tsp sugar. Serve with lemon wedges and hot sauce.
Chicken drumsticks soaked in buttermilk, dredged in seasoned flour, fried at 170C until crisp, with mash and gravy.
W: Pecans in a filling of golden syrup, brown sugar, eggs and butter, baked in shortcrust at 170C for 45 minutes, with cream.
K: sitting on the porch back home in Alabama
Black tea brewed strong, sweetened while hot, cooled and poured over ice with lemon.

s.note: Melanie's home town of Pigeon Creek
s.how: Slice 4 green tomatoes thickly and salt lightly. Dip in beaten egg, then in fine cornmeal. Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides and drain on paper. Mix mayonnaise with lemon juice and a little chopped pickle for a remoulade to serve alongside.

s.note: the local bar where Jake drinks
s.how: Toss 300g pecans with 30g melted butter, 3 tbsp brown sugar, a pinch of cayenne and sea salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 12 minutes, stirring once. Cool on the tray until glossy and crisp, then break apart.

m.how: Soak 8 chicken drumsticks in buttermilk overnight. Dredge in flour seasoned with smoked paprika and salt, then fry at 170C for 12 minutes until crisp and cooked through. Serve with buttery mash from 1kg potatoes and gravy made with chicken stock.

w.how: Line a pie dish with shortcrust and blind bake. Whisk 3 eggs with 250g golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 60g melted butter. Scatter 200g pecans in the case and pour over the filling. Bake at 170C for 45 minutes until set and serve with cream.

d.note: sitting on the porch back home in Alabama
d.how: Brew 6 black tea bags in 1L boiling water for 5 minutes and remove the bags. Stir in 150g sugar while hot, then add 1L cold water. Cool and pour over plenty of ice in tall glasses with lemon slices. Sit on the porch and drink slowly.
